risks.note: The MD&A's entire 'RISK AND CONCERNS' section is a single paragraph naming this: 'Global oversupply, softened demand from China, ongoing wars and volatile input and freight costs continued to weigh on benchmark prices.' Benchmark price weakness is what forced the company to choose margin over volume, and it is outside management's control.
risks.risk: Steel price cyclicality driven by global oversupply and weak Chinese demand

risks.note: Management flags volatile input and freight costs in the same Risk and Concerns paragraph, and separately attributes the year's margin expansion to 'tight control over power costs, scrap sourcing, and yield losses'. Since the company manufactures on 100% recycled scrap, scrap and power price moves feed straight through to the margin story the equity case now rests on.
risks.risk: Volatile input and freight costs; margin depends on scrap and power cost control

risks.note: 'Ongoing wars' is named by management as one of the factors weighing on benchmark prices, alongside freight cost volatility - both are exogenous and were flagged as continuing rather than resolved.

The company reports it 'maintained 100% capacity utilization through the year'. With the base plant already full, incremental growth cannot come from the existing asset and depends entirely on the new alloy steel capacity being commissioned.
risks.risk: No capacity headroom in the existing business

risks.note: The FY27 growth plan rests on one project: phase 1 of 100,000 MT per annum at Vaneera Industries' Ludhiana facility is stated only as 'ready to commission soon', with alloy steel facility work still 'underway' and no commissioning date, no rupee capex quantum and no funding plan disclosed in the report. The full 204,000 MT per annum licensed capacity is described as four times the company's current capacity, so the ramp is large relative to the existing business.
risks.risk: Execution and ramp-up risk on the Vaneera alloy steel project

risks.note: In its key-ratio disclosure the company explains the movement in its debt-equity ratio and debt service coverage ratio as being 'due to Increase in Borrowings during the year as compared to previous year' and 'Increase in the amount of Borrowings and their repayments during the year'. Borrowings rose from a near-debt-free base in a year in which the balance of the Vaneera consideration was paid, and further alloy-steel phases are still to be funded.

The value-added strategy deliberately concentrates the book on automotive, agri-machinery, engineering and precision industrial buyers, with the company 'established as a preferred vendor to Tier-2 OEM suppliers'. The same recurring-order relationships that support realisations also make the business sensitive to a downturn in auto and engineering demand; the report discloses no customer-concentration numbers.
risks.risk: Concentration in a narrow set of end markets and Tier-2 OEM customers

risks.note: Both the existing business and the new alloy steel facility are at Ludhiana, Punjab, and the report states 'During the year, the company has employed 55 persons.' A single manufacturing location and a headcount that small leave the company exposed to site-level disruption and to key-person dependence on the promoter-family executive directors.
risks.risk: Single-location operations and a very small workforce
